title: Games: friends panel, sign-in and a slimmer lobby — round 1

steps.headline: Signed out, Games opens with one sign-in card at the top, and Connect 4 and Chess are greyed until you sign in.
steps.changed: The banner moved to the top as a card: your sentence and a centred, filled Sign in. "Flappy and 2048 play without an account" is gone. Connect 4 and Chess are greyed.
steps.notice: Flappy and 2048 still play signed out. A greyed game can't be clicked; it still says "Sign in to play".

steps.path: Gamepad button, signed in with four friends
steps.headline: Signed in, your friends sit at the top of Games in one card, each with a status pill; games are below.
steps.changed: A friends card on top: you and Go incognito, a box to add a friend, then each friend with an Online, In game or Offline pill.
steps.notice: Everything about friends lives here now, not inside a game. The games sit below the card.

steps.path: Gamepad button, a friend request each way
steps.headline: Friend requests join the same list: someone asking shows Accept and Decline, a request you sent shows Request sent and Cancel.
steps.changed: A request to you is the first row, with Accept and Decline; one you sent is the last, with Request sent and Cancel.
steps.notice: They used to be separate cards inside each game.

steps.path: Gamepad button, signed in, no friends yet
steps.headline: With no friends yet, the card is just you, the add box and one grey line.
steps.changed: The line reads "No friends yet. Add someone by their handle and they show up here." Before, Games said nothing about friends until you opened a game.
steps.notice: Connect 4 and Chess say "No friends online" and still open.

steps.path: Games → Chess, signed in with four friends
steps.headline: A game's page is now just your friends, their status, your record against each, and Challenge.
steps.changed: Gone from the game page: your profile card, Add a friend, friend requests and the ⋯ menu. Each friend is one row: status pill, Challenge when they're online, and your record at this game in a column on the right.
steps.notice: Records line up on the right under "Your record"; a dash means you've never played them. Incoming challenges still appear at the top of this page.
steps.risk: To unfriend, block or go incognito you now go back to the Games list.

steps.path: Games → Chess, signed in, no friends yet
steps.headline: A game with no friends to play shows one card and a filled Add a friend that takes you back to the Games list.
steps.changed: Before, this page showed your profile and the add box. Now it explains, and the button goes to where adding lives.
steps.notice: The button takes you to the Games list; you then type the handle in the friends card there.

steps.path: Games → Connect 4, signed in with one friend
steps.headline: Connect 4's page at its narrower default width: one friend, online, with Challenge and a 1W - 0L record.
steps.changed: Same page as Chess, at Connect 4's 420-wide default.
steps.notice: The row fits on one line at this width.

steps.path: Phone (390 wide) → menu → Games, signed in
steps.headline: On a phone the friends card and the games fit the width; nothing scrolls sideways.
steps.changed: The same card as on a computer, at phone width; nothing scrolls sideways.
steps.notice: You scroll past your friends to reach the games.

steps.path: Phone (390 wide) → menu → Games, signed out
steps.headline: Signed out on a phone: the sign-in card on top, Connect 4 and Chess greyed underneath.
steps.changed: The signed-out card at phone width, games greyed underneath.
steps.notice: The sentence wraps to two lines; the button stays centred.

steps.headline: A game's page on a phone: the record column still lines up; a long name is shortened with dots.
steps.changed: The same rows at phone width; the record column still lines up.

steps.path: A 640 × 480 window → Games, signed in with four friends
steps.headline: In a small window the friends card fills the first screen; the games are below it, out of sight until you scroll.
steps.changed: Before, the games were the first thing you saw. Now four friends and the add box take the visible space.
steps.notice: You have to scroll to reach Flappy or 2048 in a window this small.
steps.risk: This is the main cost of friends-first; the last question asks whether to shorten the list.

steps.path: Gamepad button, signed in, game server unreachable
steps.headline: When the game server can't be reached, your status says Offline and Connect 4 and Chess are greyed with the reason.
steps.changed: Your own status reads Offline, and friends show no status pill (nobody's status is known). Connect 4 and Chess were already disabled here and keep "Can't reach the game server".

steps.path: Gamepad button, signed in, a request each way
steps.headline: How should adding a friend fit into the friends card?
steps.notice: Whichever you pick is the only place to add a friend; games no longer have their own add box.

variants.label: Box at the top
variants.summary: The handle box is always there, under your own line, like Session details' Add a tag. One step: type and press Add.

variants.label: Button under the list
variants.summary: A full-width outlined Add a friend under the list opens the box in its place. A calmer card; one extra click.
variants.risk: With a long list the button sits far down the card.

variants.label: Fold-out row
variants.summary: An Add a friend row with an arrow, like every fold-out in Settings; it opens the box underneath.
variants.risk: Reads like a setting rather than an action.

steps.headline: Should the signed-out Sign in be a centred button, as you asked, or full width, as the design guide says?
steps.notice: The guide says a lone button is full width unless it sits beside its text; your direction said centred. Your pick settles which rule wins here.

variants.label: Centred
variants.summary: A filled Sign in under the centred sentence, as wide as its word.

variants.label: Full width
variants.summary: The same filled button across the card, like the Account popup's sign-in card.

steps.path: Games → Chess, signed in with four friends
steps.headline: How should a game's page show your record against each friend?
steps.notice: The same look will be used in Chess and Connect 4.

variants.label: Score column
variants.summary: "4W - 2L - 1D" at the right edge under a "Your record" label, like the scores on Flappy's and 2048's boards. A dash when you've never played.

variants.label: Chip by the name
variants.summary: Today's look: a small record chip after the status pill. Nothing shows for someone you've never played.
variants.risk: Chips don't line up from row to row.

variants.label: Sentence under the name
variants.summary: "You lead 4–2 (1 draw)", "Mira leads 3–1", "All square at 2–2", "Not played yet" in grey under each name, the wording the end-of-game card uses.

steps.path: Gamepad button, signed in with many friends
steps.headline: When you have many friends, should the friends card show only some of them so the games stay in view?
steps.today: The draft lists every friend, online first, then the games underneath. In a 640 × 480 window four friends already push the games out of sight.
steps.problem: Someone with twenty friends would scroll past all of them every time they just want to play Flappy.
steps.proposal: Keep the card short and put the rest one click away, or leave it as drafted.

options.label: Show everyone
pros: Everyone is visible at a glance
cons: Games can end up far down the panel

options.label: Online first, rest folded
pros: The friends you can play now stay on top
The card stays short most of the time
cons: Offline friends, their ⋯ menu and Last seen need one click

options.label: First five, then Show all
cons: Might hide someone online if more than five are
